summary:
Our project, Abandoned but not Forgotten: NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars, is an interactive book designed for children who are interested in space. We developed this book to tell the stories of the different machines, rovers, and scientific instruments that NASA has left on the Moon and Mars after completing their missions. It explains what each object was designed to do, how it worked, what discoveries it helped make, and what happened to it after its mission ended.

Our project addresses the challenge by turning scientific information into an educational and interactive experience. Instead of only presenting facts, we want children to explore the stories behind this equipment and understand its role in space exploration.

This project is important because many of these objects are forgotten once their missions are over, even though they helped scientists make important discoveries. We want to inspire young readers to become more curious about science, technology, and the exploration of space.
details:
Our project is a digital interactive book designed to teach children about NASA's equipment left on the Moon and Mars. It works by taking readers through different pages where they can discover machines, rovers, and scientific instruments that were part of past space missions. Each section includes simple explanations, illustrations, interesting facts, and interactive activities to make learning more enjoyable.

One of its main benefits is that it makes scientific information easier for children to understand. It also encourages curiosity, creativity, and interest in space exploration. Our goal is to help young readers understand that even equipment left behind has an important story and helped scientists make discoveries.

We used Canva to create the book, including its illustrations, interactive elements, and activities. Our project is creative because it combines storytelling, science, and interactive learning instead of presenting information only as text.

While developing our idea, we considered the age of our audience, the importance of using accurate information, simple language, attractive illustrations, and activities that keep children interested. We also wanted the book to be easy to access and use.
